gaps.sentence: Little did the suspects ___ that the police were listening.
gaps.explanation: 'Little did they know' — 'know' as bare verb after the inverted auxiliary 'did'.

gaps.sentence: ___ I known about the change of plan, I would have waited.
gaps.explanation: 'Had I known …' = 'If I had known …' — inverted third conditional.

gaps.sentence: Only after the third reminder ___ she reply to my email.
gaps.explanation: 'Only after' fronts the condition, so 'did she reply' inverts.

gaps.sentence: So loud ___ the music that the neighbours called the police.
gaps.explanation: 'So loud was the music that …' — fronted 'so + adj' with inversion.

gaps.sentence: Not once ___ she mentioned the incident to anyone.
gaps.explanation: 'Not once has she mentioned' — inversion with the perfect.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ she apologise, she also paid for the damage.
gaps.explanation: Not only did she…, (but) she also… — inversion after not only.

gaps.sentence: Not since the winter of 1963 ___ temperatures dropped so low.
gaps.explanation: 'Not since 1963 have temperatures dropped …' — the only time from then until now.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the play cancelled, but the theatre was closed as well.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only was the play cancelled' — inverted passive.
